title: Annotatio IV §.XII: Rom 1 applied — glory of God exchanged for images and bread-foam
pass_a_gloss: so much so that to the Christian Church of that Age, considered for the greater part, there ought to be applied what Paul writes concerning the Gentiles to the Romans: Because although they knew God, yet they did not glorify Him as God, but became vain in their reasonings and their Heart was darkened, lacking understanding; when they call themselves Wise, they became fools and changed the glory of the incorruptible GOD into fashioned images of every kind and the foam of bread, someday to be adored by their posterity.
pass_b_english: So far that Paul’s charge against the Gentiles (Romans) fits most of this age’s Christian Church:

Knowing God they did not glorify Him; claiming to be wise they became fools and exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God for fashioned images of every kind — and the foam of bread for posterity to adore.
source_text: adeo, ut Christianæ istius Seculi Ecclesiæ, ex majori sui parte consideratæ, applicari illud debeat, quod Paulus de Ethnicis ad Romanos scribit: Proptereà, quòd cùm Deum noverint, tamen ut Deum non glorificaverunt, sed vani facti sunt in ratiocinationibus suis & obtenebratum est Cor eorum, intelligentiâ carens, cùm se dictitant Sapientes, stulti facti sunt & mutarunt gloriam DEI incorruptibilis in efformatas omnis generis imagines panisque spumam, olim à posteris suis adorandam.
